en: Thus have I heard— Majjhima Nikāya 134: The Discourse to Lomasakaṅgiya on the Single Excellent Night.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Park.
Then the young deva Candana, in the late night, with a magnificent radiance, illuminated the entire Nigrodha Park.
Having illuminated [the area], he approached the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya and stood to one side.
Standing to one side, the young deva Candana said this to the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya:
“Bhikkhu, do you maintain the summary and the exposition of the ‘One Fortunate Night’?”
“Friend, I do not remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Fortunate Night.
But do you, friend, remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Fortunate Night’?
“I too, monk, do not remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Fortunate Night.’”
“But do you, monk, remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses?
“I do not, friend, remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses.
But do you, friend, remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses?”
“I do indeed remember, monk, the *Bhaddekaratta* verses.
“But how, friend, do you remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses?
“Once, monk, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Tāvatiṃsa devas at the foot of the Pāricchattaka tree on the yellow sandalwood stone.”
There, the Blessed One recited the summary and the exposition of the "Blessing of a Single Night" for the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven:
"One should not pursue the past,
nor should one long for the future;”
That which is past is abandoned;
that which is future has not yet been reached;
and as for the phenomenon that is present—
Therein, one sees with insight;
the wise person should cultivate that which is immovable and unshakable.
Today itself one should exert oneself in what is to be done;
who knows if death will come tomorrow?
For we have no appointment with it.
By Death, who possesses a great army.
Thus dwelling, ardent,
untiring day and night—
“The Sage who is at peace indeed declares that this is ‘One Fortunate Night.
It is in this way, monk, that I remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses.
"Learn, monk, the summary and the exposition of 'One Fortunate Night';
master, monk, the summary and the exposition of 'One Fortunate Night';
memorize, monk, the summary and the exposition of 'One Fortunate Night'."
“Bhikkhu, this summary and exposition of ‘One Fortunate Night,’ which is conducive to welfare and forms the foundation of the holy life,” said the young deva Candana.
Having said this, he vanished right there.
Then, at the end of that night, the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya put his lodging in order, took his bowl and robe, and set out on a wandering tour toward Sāvatthī.
Traveling by stages on his tour, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthī, at Jetavana, the monastery of Anāthapiṇḍika, where the Blessed One was staying.
Having approached the Blessed One and paid homage to him, he sat down to one side. To one side...
Seated, the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya said this to the Blessed One:
“Once, Bhante, I was staying among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Nigrodha Monastery.
Then, Bhante, a certain son of the gods, having arrived when the night was far spent, with a most excellent complexion, [illuminating] the entire [monastery]...”
Having illuminated the Nigrodha Park, that son of the gods approached me and stood to one side.
Standing there, venerable sir, he said this to me:
“Bhikkhu, do you remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Excellent Night’?”
When this was said, venerable sir, I said to that young god:
“Friend, I do not remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night.
But do you, friend, remember the summary and the exposition of ‘One Who Has Had a Single Excellent Night’?”
“Monk, I too do not remember the summary and the detailed exposition of the *Bhaddekaratta* discourse.
But do you, monk, remember the verses of the *Bhaddekaratta*? “I do not remember them, friend.”
“But do you, friend, remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses?
“I do indeed, bhikkhu, remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses.
“But how, friend, do you remember the *Bhaddekaratta* verses?”
“On one occasion, bhikkhu, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Tāvatiṃsa devas at the foot of the Pāricchattaka tree upon the yellow sandalwood stone.
There, the Blessed One recited the summary and the exposition of the ‘Blessed Single Night’ for the Tāvatiṃsa devas:
‘One should not pursue the past;’”
"That indeed is called 'the one auspicious night,' so the peaceful Sage has declared."
"It is in this way, monk, that I remember the verses on 'One Excellent Night.
You too, monk, should learn the summary and the exposition of 'One Excellent Night';
you should master the summary and the exposition of 'One Excellent Night.'"
“Bhikkhu, you should master both the summary and the exposition of ‘One Fortunate Night.
Bhikkhu, the summary and the exposition of ‘One Fortunate Night’ are beneficial and pertain to the fundamentals of the holy life.
This is what that son of the gods said, venerable sir.
Having said this, he vanished right there.
“It would be well, Bhante, if the Blessed One would teach me the summary and the exposition of ‘One Fortunate Night.
“But do you know that son of the gods, bhikkhu?”
“I do not know that son of the gods, venerable sir.
“That son of the gods is named Candana, bhikkhu.
Candana, bhikkhu, listens to the Dhamma having made it his bone, having attended to it, having focused his whole mind upon it, and with his ear bent forward.”
"In that case, bhikkhu, listen and attend closely; I shall speak.
"Yes, venerable sir," the Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“One should not pursue the past,
nor long for the future;
what is past has been relinquished.”
And that which has not yet been reached, the future;
and whatever phenomenon is present—
one who discerns them each in their respective place;
Unshakable and unagitated—
let the wise man cultivate that.
What is to be done should be done with diligence this very day.
Who knows when death will come tomorrow?
For we have no agreement with that Death who possesses a vast army.
One who dwells thus,
ardent and untiring by day and night—
him indeed they call "Bhaddekaratta."
The sage who is virtuous explains this:
"And how, bhikkhu, does one pursue the past? ... [as above] ...
In this way, bhikkhu, one pursues the past.
And how, bhikkhu, does one not pursue the past? ... [as before] ...
In this way, bhikkhu, one does not pursue the past.
And how, bhikkhu, does one long for the future? ... [as before] ...
In this way, bhikkhu, one longs for the future.
And how, bhikkhu, does one not long for the future? ... [as before] ...
In this way, bhikkhu, one does not long for the future.
And how, bhikkhu, is one carried away by present phenomena? ... [as before] ...
In this way, bhikkhu, one is carried away by present phenomena.
And how, bhikkhu, is one not shaken regarding present phenomena?
… [as before] … In this way, bhikkhu, one is not shaken regarding present phenomena.
One should not pursue the past.
One should not long for the future;
for that which is past has been abandoned,
and that which is future has not yet arrived.
And whoever discerns, here and there, the phenomenon of the present—
unshakable and unshakeable—
Knowing this, one should cultivate it.
Diligence is to be practiced this very day;
who knows if death will come tomorrow?
For we have made no compact with that Death who leads a great army.
[We do not fear] one who dwells thus, ardent and vigilant.
“Unwearied by day and night—
him indeed the peaceful Sage calls ‘One Fortunate Night.’”
Thus the Blessed One spoke.
The Venerable Lomasakaṅgiya, being uplifted, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Bhaddekaratta Sutta with Lomasakaṅgiya, the fourth, is concluded.
